statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail moves back up from 21 to 24 because the 29,267.42 recovery high has been rejected and the index has faded into the lower third of the day range, while VIX prints a new session high. Tail remains one point below the block threshold.

headline: Nasdaq-100 rejects the 29,267 bounce high and fades to 29,078 as VIX sets a session high, the 10-year holds 4.786% and WTI stays near $89.95
body:
The change this hour is that the recovery documented at the previous assessment has been given back. At 16:25 UTC the index was 29,143.98 having just printed a 29,267.42 session high; at 17:26 UTC it is 29,078.48. That retraces roughly two thirds of the 275-point bounce off the 28,992.25 low and puts price back in the lower third of the day range. Nasdaq-100 futures tell the same story at 29,161.00, well beneath a 29,571.25 session high.

Cross-asset alignment has re-formed rather than decayed. VIX is 16.10 with a new session high of 16.13, above the 16.06 high that stood an hour ago, so the volatility premium that faded during the midday recovery is rebuilding. The U.S. 10-year is 4.786%, within four basis points of its 4.790% day high and reported as the highest intraday level since January 2025, while the 30-year around 5.26% sits near multi-decade highs. WTI is $89.52, up 4.38%, holding just under its $89.95 high. Gold is down 1.97% at $4,393.40, which is unusual alongside an equity decline and points to a rates-driven rather than a pure risk-aversion move.

The underlying drivers are two and they are compounding. First, a global bond sell-off: the Japanese 10-year briefly touched 3% for the first time in three decades, and long-end yields are elevated across several markets. Second, renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, where two tankers, one Saudi-owned and one South Korean-owned, were struck by projectiles on Monday evening, rebuilding an energy risk premium. Today's U.S. data was firm rather than weak, with ISM Manufacturing at 54.6, JOLTS openings at 7.271 million and construction spending at -0.5%, which does nothing to relieve the yield pressure.

On the Tail measure specifically, the case for staying below the block threshold rests on structure. A 275-point retracement genuinely occurred this session, the 28,992.25 low has not been retested let alone broken, and the move from the high has been a fade rather than an accelerating extension. The case against is the amplifier stack: yields at day highs, crude near day highs, VIX at a session high, semiconductors uniformly negative and an unresolved geopolitical channel. Weighing an observed two-sided range against an aligned but not yet path-confirmed backdrop gives Tail 24 and Stress 73.

The danger window is narrowed to the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour, where close mechanics and the unresolved shock make a range retest most likely to convert into a directional close. Conditional Tail there is 26. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 15:34 UTC and is beyond the 90-minute freshness bound for this run, so it was not used as material evidence; the assessment rests on directly verified current sources.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 UTC hour on 1 September has none and is marked unavailable. The first fifteen slots, covering the 31 August U.S. session and the overnight hours into 1 September, all sat in the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 50 up to 58 as crude firmed and long yields climbed. The regime changed at 08:00 UTC on 1 September, when Tail moved to 22 with mode trend-down. It reached 26 at 09:00 UTC for the first BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES reading, held 25 through 10:00 and 11:00 UTC, then rose to 28 at 12:00 UTC and peaked at 31 with Stress 75 at 13:00 UTC, the highest Tail of the sequence. The 14:00 UTC assessment cut Tail to 24 and changed mode to event/whipsaw once the index retraced off its low, and 16:00 UTC eased further to 21 after a 29,267.42 higher high. Confidence stayed between 84 and 89 throughout, so the sequence reflects a genuine regime change rather than deteriorating evidence quality.
outlookSummary: The projection starts from a rejected bounce rather than from either an extension or a holding recovery, so Tail opens at 24 for the current 17:00 UTC hour, one point under the block threshold. It lifts to 26 for the 19:00 UTC power hour, the single declared danger window, where close mechanics plus an unresolved crude and rates shock most plausibly convert a range retest into a directional close; that lift is a scheduled structural allowance and not an observed path. Tail returns to 24 through the 20:00 UTC cash close, then falls to 21 and into the EA_ON band from 22:00 UTC as the impulse is assumed to decay overnight, bottoming at 13 through the Asian afternoon. It rebuilds gradually through the European session and lifts to 19 for the 12:00 UTC ADP employment hour on 2 September, 20 for the digestion hour, and 22 for the 14:00 UTC U.S. cash open, the projection's second-highest reading, because the opening auction is structurally where an overnight imbalance can become a directional session, as it did on 1 September. Confidence declines steadily from 88 to 62 across the series, which reflects distance from observed evidence rather than any deterioration in the current evidence base. Every reading beyond the current hour is conditional; the named invalidation is a decisive loss of the 28,992.25 session low, and the named upside condition is an orderly hold above it with volatility decay.
